-1.60000,12.20000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-87.67180,41.86950.name: University of Illinois at Chicago IVF Program
-87.67180,41.86950.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Frank Gonzalez, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-84.35356,40.70894.name: Charles River Laboratories - Spencerville
-84.35356,40.70894.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-64.80029,46.09404.name: Oulton College
-64.80029,46.09404.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, May 2026
-64.80029,46.09404.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, May 2026. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-77.42232,39.44038.name: Integrated Research Facility at Fort Detrick (IRF - Detrick)
-77.42232,39.44038.state: 8200 Research Plaza, Fort Detrick, Maryland 21702, United States
-77.42232,39.44038.company: National Institutes of Health, Department of Health and Human Services. Operated by Battelle Memorial Institute, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) until March 2020, since then operated by Laulima Government Solutions LLC (Jens Kuhn)
-77.42232,39.44038.desc: A BSL4 animal laboratory, operational. Run by National Institutes of Health, Department of Health and Human Services. Operated by Battelle Memorial Institute, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) until March 2020, since then operated by Laulima Government Solutions LLC (Jens Kuhn). It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in full-body positive-pressure suits with their own air supply. Containment space: 1305 SqM. Operational or announced: 2013. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-0.12000,52.21300.name: Genus / PIC
-0.12000,52.21300.state: Basingstoke, UK — Matrix House, Basing View
-0.12000,52.21300.desc: The world’s largest pig genetics company, supplying breeding stock across dozens of countries, and the developer of pigs edited to resist PRRS — a disease that spreads because pigs are kept in crowded conditions. Its position means an edit approved once propagates through a very large share of global pig production within a few generations. The crowding does not change; the animal is rewritten to tolerate it.

-77.10050,38.99580.name: ClinicalTrials.gov — sponsor and site search
-77.10050,38.99580.desc: The searchable interface to the trial register, by sponsor, site and condition. It is how the clinical facet of this map is compiled at all: 26,240 gene and cell therapy trials, 6,088 lead sponsors, from a public register that exists because a law requires it.

2.29600,49.89400.name: Ỹnsect
2.29600,49.89400.desc: Farms mealworms at industrial scale for animal feed and pet food, with selective breeding and genomic selection applied to the insects themselves. Insect farming is regulated as agriculture rather than as biotechnology, so breeding programmes on a species nobody has domesticated before proceed with very little oversight.

127.03500,37.48700.name: Macrogen
127.03500,37.48700.desc: A large service sequencing provider across Asia, and one of the operators behind national genome projects in the region. Regional providers are how countries without their own capacity get sequencing done, and they inherit the question of where the resulting data sits.
